For the people who missed the AMA.

What the MiniMax H3 Team Actually Said: 10 Answers From the Reddit AMA

MiniMax H3 launched as a unified multimodal video model that can process text, images, video and audio in one context. MiniMax says it can generate up to 15 seconds of video with native stereo sound at resolutions up to 2K. (MiniMax announcement)

In a Reddit AMA, the H3 research and engineering team answered questions about the public release, upcoming features, local inference and the model’s current weaknesses. These are the ten replies that matter most.

1. H3-Regenerate-2K will be released, but there is no date yet

Kiro confirmed that MiniMax plans to open-source H3-Regenerate-2K.

It is not simply the current H3 checkpoint running a second time, and it is not a conventional pixel-space upscaler. The module uses a dedicated latent-space DiT regeneration checkpoint that targets a higher resolution. The original H3 output becomes additional context, while some reference inputs can also be supplied at higher resolution.

MiniMax is still improving its efficiency and quality for local use, so the team has not announced a release date. (Kiro’s reply)

2. H3 does not use MiniMax M3’s MSA attention system

The team clarified that H3 does not use the MSA system from MiniMax M3.

Its approach is closer to MoBA-style block selection. Neighboring visual tokens are grouped into blocks, and mean-pooled representations are used to estimate which blocks are important. The model can then avoid spending the same amount of attention on every visual token.

The current design applies three-dimensional sparsification to video tokens. Image and text tokens may be included later. MiniMax plans to release a conservative reference implementation, with the first goal being no noticeable quality loss. The best speed improvements will still depend on hardware and backend optimization by the community. (Kiro’s sparse-attention reply)

3. A faster or smaller official model is being considered, but not promised

The released checkpoint already includes CFG distillation and can operate with fewer inference steps than a completely undistilled model.

However, it was not specifically trained for extreme low-step generation. MiniMax is exploring further step distillation and is considering versions using four or eight NFE, but the team did not commit to releasing one soon.

Kiro also said there is no near-term plan for a separately trained smaller T2V or I2V version. Instead, the team expects the community may derive smaller variants through structured block pruning, recovery training or distillation. (Kiro’s efficiency replies)

4. The team knows about pixelation on small and distant subjects

One user asked why people and objects often become pixelated or distorted when they are far from the camera.

Kiro confirmed that MiniMax has observed the same problem, especially with small or distant subjects. The team does not believe it can be explained simply by the Visual VAE’s compression ratio or by one specific training stage.

They described it as a system-level issue involving several parts of the model and training pipeline. Improving it will be one of their next priorities. The AMA did not provide a sampler, scheduler or step-count setting that reliably solves the problem. (Kiro’s reply about distant subjects)

5. MiniMax is developing a dedicated image-generation model

H3 can already produce useful still images through video-based workarounds, but MiniMax is developing a proper image model from a common ancestor in the H3 model family.

The new model will reuse H3’s VAE encoder. Because the temporal encoder is causal, MiniMax can obtain a two-dimensional VAE encoder through weight slicing. The team also plans to build a dedicated VAE decoder for image generation.

Kiro also clarified that H3 is not a streaming video model. It cannot generate a preview frame, wait for approval and then continue the same generation into a video. The intended workflow is to create the first frame with the future image model and then send it to H3’s I2VA mode. (Kiro’s image-model reply)

6. Ref2Vid quality problems are partly caused by the model itself

Many users noticed that Ref2Vid can look softer and less stable than I2V, especially when a driving video is used as the reference.

Nero confirmed that MiniMax is aware of the issue. The FL2VA and Ref2VA checkpoints currently have different visual-quality tendencies because they used different post-training strategies. The team is actively working on improving Ref2VA.

The practical advice was simple: use the highest-quality reference input available. Ref2VA is sensitive to the quality of its reference conditioning, so a poor or compressed reference can make the result worse. (Nero’s Ref2VA reply)

7. H3’s prompt adherence does not come from one special trick

When asked why H3 follows detailed prompts so well, the team did not point to one special architectural feature.

The answer from dacongya was that the most important factors were a broad and diverse set of data and tasks, a general-purpose architecture, and avoiding design choices that do not scale effectively.

MiniMax did not disclose the size of the training dataset. The broader point was that H3’s instruction-following comes from the combination of data construction, task design, architecture and training strategy. (dacongya’s reply)

8. A simple video-training task produced strong image-editing ability

Nero described one experiment that changed how he thought about video models.

The team trained a model on a simple task: provide the first frame and a caption, then predict the final frame. Even without image-editing-specific post-training, the model achieved strong zero-shot results across several image-editing benchmarks.

This suggested that natural-language in-context learning can generalize across different generation tasks. It also helps explain why H3 can sometimes perform editing and composition tasks that were not presented as separate headline features at launch. (Nero’s training observation)

9. Local users can approximate Context-IR with official guides

The full native Context-IR experience remains available through MiniMax’s API, but the team has provided tools for local users.

Luigi pointed users to separate official guides for the base workflow and the reference workflow. Both include prompt-expansion instructions and structured input examples. MiniMax has also combined the material into an H3 Prompt Writing Skill and plans to keep updating it.

This does not reproduce the complete online Context-IR pipeline, but it gives local users a clearer way to structure complex prompts and multimodal references.

The resources are available in the base prompt guide, the reference prompt guide, and the H3 Prompt Writing Skill. (Luigi’s reply)

10. Longer videos are possible, but seamless continuation is still experimental

Nero explained that Ref2VA can use the ending section of a previous video and its audio as references for the next segment. The user then describes how the new segment should continue.

However, this method does not guarantee a seamless transition. Identity drift, motion discontinuity and other changes can still appear.

The team also discussed an unofficial RoPE-extension workflow inherited from pretraining. It may produce better continuation in some cases, but it requires stricter prompting and is not reliably compatible with multiple reference inputs.

MiniMax originally trained a dedicated audio-video continuation task with extended RoPE positions. It worked well as a standalone task, but did not generalize as strongly when combined with many other tasks. The released model therefore relies mainly on standard reference conditioning and has not been natively trained on long recurrent chains. The team believes long-trajectory training combined with sparse attention could improve this in the future. (Nero’s continuation replies)

The main takeaway

The AMA gave a fairly specific picture of where H3 is going.

MiniMax plans to release the 2K regeneration module and a sparse-attention implementation. The team is exploring four-step and eight-step inference, while a separate smaller model is not currently planned. A dedicated image model is in development, and the official prompt guides are already available.

At the same time, Ref2VA quality, distant subjects, local prompt processing and long-video continuation still have clear limitations.

The most important point is that open weights are only one part of the system. H3’s core model is available, but the complete production pipeline, high-resolution regeneration and inference optimizations are still being developed. The next stage will depend as much on the surrounding tools and community work as on the model weights themselves.

⚡️ Here's how to use the "more details" button in Codex app to offload stuff to 5.6 on web and save a bunch of codex usage limits at the same time.

Basic pattern:

1. highlight something in the codex app response, click "more details". esp useful is having codex specifically write a "handoff" just for this purpose, then highlight it all -> "more details"

2. your thread context + your highlighted text get sent to a quick chat -> this uses your web chatgpt quota, not codex limits -> ask it anything, esp useful is research/planning type asks with 5.6 Pro or xhigh thinking.

HUGE: this allows you to access 5.6 pro from within Codex w/o copy/paste.

3. along with research/planning you can also have it create image mockups or other artifacts as per your tasks' needs, from your context.

4. when you're ready to bring that external context back into codex, press the "add to task" button in the quick chat window header to re-inject that context back into your codex thread.

5. ask codex thread to integrate that context into its own work (i.e, merge that research in to draft a final plan)

Use this workflow as needed without burning your codex limits, rinse and repeat.

Rather than optimizing a diffusion policy with unstable RL objectives, EvoHIL combines a self-evolving reward model with flow matching optimization.

The policy learns from better rewards, while better policies generate stronger preference data for the next reward update. Each component bootstraps the other.
